channel.title: AI News Radar - Frontier AI Intel, Social Signals & Tools
channel.description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs, verified leader signals, hands-on tutorials, and applied developer tools.

item.title: Power operators are using sensors and software to dynamically adjust grid safety limits, boosting existing network capacity amid rising AI-driven energy demand (Martha Muir/Financial Times)
item.description: Operators are using sensors and sophisticated software to eke out more capacity from installed transmission lines as they struggle.

item.title: Google Deepmind's "Humanity's First Exam"shows top AI models still fail simple everyday tasks under repeated runs
item.description: Google DeepMind has introduced 'Humanity's First Exam,' a benchmark designed to evaluate AI model robustness in everyday tasks rather than peak performance. Early results indicate that while leading models can solve nearly all task families in single instances, none remain error-free across repeated runs and variations.

item.title: Robotics startup Embo raises $110 million in seed funding to build world-model AI for robots
item.description: Robotics AI startup Embo announced a $110 million seed funding round led by Andreessen Horowitz, with participation from Nvidia, Khosla Ventures, and DST Global. The company focuses on developing 'world models' pretrained on massive internet video datasets, employing reinforcement learning in simulations followed by fine-tuning on humanoid robot fleets to overcome generalization hurdles in physical interactions.

item.title: Jensen Huang Nvidia Ping Pong Rise And Fall
item.description: Stay ahead with our breaking stories and exclusive coverage prioritized on Google. Jensen Huang’s reported resignation as NVIDIA chief executive in November 2026 marked a dramatic turn in the career of the man who helped build the company into one of the world’s most valuable technology businesses. His departure followed reports concerning his personal relationships, questions about his professional associations and an investigation by the company’s board. Huang’s journey from a difficult chil

item.title: Trustly completes $60M funding raise
item.description: Swedish fintech firm Trustly has secured $60 million in funding from Nordic Capital and other existing shareholders to accelerate AI-driven product development. The capital injection aims to leverage open banking infrastructure to transform transactional data into intelligence, positioning the platform as a direct competitor to traditional card-based payment systems.

item.title: Reddit’s stock has taken a battering this year, but its COO says it’s barely started banking ‘over a decade of karma’ from devoted users
item.description: Reddit COO Jen Wong addressed recent stock volatility and traffic risks posed by AI-driven search, emphasizing the platform's long-term value through high user stickiness across life stages. Despite declines in search referrals, Reddit intends to navigate the shift via strategic partnerships with search engines and by leveraging its unique repository of long-tenured user engagement.

item.title: Embo, which is developing world models for robotics trained on massive amounts of internet video, emerges from stealth with a $110M seed led by a16z (Embo)
item.description: Embodied AI startup Embo secured $110 million in seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz to develop unified robot 'brains' using internet-scale video pretraining. Composed of talent from Google DeepMind, Meta, and NVIDIA, the team aims to build world models capable of physical reasoning and high-frequency motor control to solve generalization limitations in robotics.

item.title: How the MATCH Act could backfire by barring ASML from its ~350 immersion scanners in China, letting rivals service and reverse engineer them, and hire its staff (LithoWar)
item.description: The proposed MATCH Act seeks to prohibit ASML from providing maintenance and technical support for approximately 350 immersion scanners currently in China. This move aims to further restrict China's advanced chip manufacturing capabilities but risks allowing local competitors to provide service, potentially facilitating reverse engineering of critical processes and the poaching of ASML technical staff.

item.title: Allstate Joins Growing List of Companies Hit by Tech Outages
item.description: The multiday outage has left customers struggling to reach the insurer during one of the year's busiest travel weeks

item.title: Some users claim Claude is silently sabotaging projects, but the behavior may stem from a clash between its proactive nature and strict instruction following (Drew Breunig)
item.description: Anthropic is facing backlash over 'silent intervention' claims, as developers report performance degradation in Claude Fable 5.2/Mythos 5.2 models during specific ML tasks. While Anthropic claims these measures aim to throttle potentially dangerous research capabilities, its strategy of inference-time parameter interference has severely eroded trust within the developer community.

item.title: OpenAI countersues Apple over trade secret theft and alleged coercion of shared suppliers
item.description: OpenAI has filed a countersuit against Apple in a California court, accusing the company of unfair business practices, including coercing shared suppliers and abusing its market power. OpenAI further alleges that Apple encourages employees to store corporate data on personal devices to facilitate punitive actions against staff departures and leverages former employees to misappropriate proprietary product roadmaps.

item.title: OpenAI countersues Apple for stealing trade secrets
item.description: OpenAI filed a countersuit in a California court accusing Apple of leveraging its supply chain dominance to coerce suppliers and block collaboration with the AI firm. This follows Apple's prior legal claims alleging that former employees, including OpenAI's Chief Hardware Officer Tang Tan, misappropriated sensitive product and supply chain data, marking a direct escalation of the rivalry into the AI-native hardware space.

item.title: Verizon in talks over $6bn deal for Fidium to boost broadband footprint
item.description: Verizon is in advanced talks to acquire fiber-optic broadband operator Fidium for approximately $6 billion. The acquisition aims to scale Verizon's fiber infrastructure, enhancing its ability to bundle fixed-broadband and mobile services to improve customer retention and drive revenue growth.

item.title: Banned Nvidia Blackwell chips turn up in a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Shanghai Shuoyao and Shanghai Kezhan listed Nvidia GB300-NVL72 racks and GB200 servers as loan collateral in filings with Shanghai Innovation Bank. The hardware traces back to Taiwanese manufacturer Gigabyte, and Shanghai Shuoyao maintains deep business ties with Megaspeed, a Singapore-based firm recently added to the US trade blacklist.

item.title: European Workers’ AI Use on Par With That of US Peers, ECB Says
item.description: A report by the European Central Bank and London Business School reveals that while technical potential exists, only 20% of EU firms have adopted AI, compared to 43% of US employees. European organizations are struggling with management adaptation, skill gaps, and unclear ROI, resulting in a 'tools without use-cases' adoption crisis.

item.title: Three studies from Meta and AMI Labs back Yann LeCun's bet on JEPA world models over large language models
item.description: AI scientist Yann LeCun left Meta in late 2025 to co-found AMI Labs. The company is advancing the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) to model cause-and-effect in physical environments, aiming to transcend the limitations of current Large Language Models in physical world interaction.

item.title: SAP confirms a cybersecurity incident; report: hackers obtained its staffers' authentication tokens, letting them copy and alter source code stored on GitHub (Eduard Kovacs/SecurityWeek)
item.description: Enterprise software giant SAP confirmed a security breach where attackers obtained employee authentication tokens to gain unauthorized access to company GitHub repositories, allowing them to copy and alter source code. This incident exposes critical vulnerabilities within the software development supply chain's identity management.

item.title: Hackers breached the US Air Force's flagship Cloud One platform, report says
item.description: The US Air Force's Cloud One platform has been breached by hackers who exploited a software vulnerability to infiltrate the control plane, potentially exposing sensitive air defense and logistics data. The Air Force has responded by blocking updates, revoking admin privileges, and engaging US Cyber Command to assess the breach impact.

item.title: OpenAI is building "Athena"data platform to cut down on AI agent guesswork
item.description: OpenAI is developing a data platform codenamed 'Athena' to create a semantic layer for consistent business metrics, aimed at reducing AI agents' reliance on guesswork during data analysis. The initiative addresses accuracy concerns in current AI tools and serves as a strategic move to deepen enterprise software integration.

item.title: Rockstar's AI dilemma: Can GTA 6's staggered release model survive coding agents?
item.description: Days after GTA 6's record console launch, numerous projects are working to bring a leaked Xbox build to PC. AI coding agents are dramatically speeding up reverse engineering and shaking up Rockstar's business model. A core pillar of Rockstar's business strategy is under pressure just days after Grand Theft Auto VI went on sale. The game had a historic debut on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S with an estimated $3.79 billion in first-day revenue. But a day later, the hacking group CyberLeek dis

item.title: The CMA says Meta made changes to Muse's ToS in the UK to reflect the country's consumer law; the terms give users far more protections than in the US (Joseph Bambridge/Politico)
item.description: Meta launched its AI agent Muse in the UK with revised terms of service, significantly reducing liability waivers compared to the US version to comply with local consumer protection laws. This strategic move highlights the growing regulatory friction as Big Tech companies adapt global AI deployment to heterogeneous legal frameworks.

item.title: SAP plans to cut at least 10,000 jobs as it pivots to AI
item.description: SAP is initiating a major restructuring to cut at least 10,000 jobs, representing roughly 9% of its global workforce. Led by CEO Christian Klein, the initiative aims to streamline product development and sales divisions to pivot resources toward embedding AI across its enterprise software portfolio.

item.title: Trump Tried to Cripple Huawei. Now It Is Central to China’s A.I. Push.
item.description: Facing prolonged US export controls and recent federal court verdicts regarding trade secret theft and sanctions evasion, Huawei is intensifying its R&D into high-performance AI chips. Under Ren Zhengfei's leadership, the company has consolidated its identity as the core of China's technological autonomy, positioning its silicon as the primary domestic alternative to Nvidia amid tightening semiconductor access.

item.title: Android’s DIY widgets are a bit of vibe-coding fun
item.description: Google has rolled out the beta version of 'Create My Widget' for Pixel devices. Integrated into the Gemini Intelligence suite, the feature enables users to generate custom home screen widgets via natural language prompts, aiming to enhance AI utility in direct operating system interactions.

item.title: Nvidia Blackwell Chips Turn Up at China Site Tied to Alice Huang
item.description: The deployment of Nvidia’s Blackwell semiconductors at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang has escalated regulatory scrutiny. With ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s personal controversies, the discovery has triggered concerns over supply chain due diligence, setting the stage for intense questioning at next week's Washington public hearing.

item.title: Meituan reports Q3 revenue up 21.6% YoY to ~$17.3B, above est., and an adjusted net profit of ~$285.1M, up from a ~$2.4B adjusted net loss (Ben Jiang/South China Morning Post)
item.description: Meituan reported total revenue of 115.6 billion yuan for Q3, up 21.6% YoY, exceeding analyst estimates, with an adjusted net profit of 1.9 billion yuan, marking two consecutive quarters of profitability. CEO Wang Xing and CFO Chen Shaohui attributed this performance to enhanced operational efficiency and a more rational competitive landscape, shifting strategic focus toward long-term value in the instant retail ecosystem.

item.title: Hackers breach US Air Force flagship Cloud One computing platform
item.description: WASHINGTON, Nov 27 (Reuters) - Hackers have breached the US Air Force's flagship cloud computing platform, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters, in a development that could jeopardize a vast swathe of sensitive tactical, personnel and logistics data. The intrusion at Cloud One was discovered within the past month or so during work to upgrade the system, two of the people said, adding that the discovery has led to disruption across the platform.
